title: TractorFacet omits Invariable fundsSafu net that sibling entrypoints enforce
description: Beanstalk applies a consistent guard architecture: every external writing facet inherits `Invariable` and wraps fund-touching logic in solvency/flow modifiers. The two arbitrary/batch execution wrappers FarmFacet (`farm`, `advancedFarm`) and DepotFacet (`pipe`, `multiPipe`, `advancedPipe`, `etherPipe`) both inherit Invariable and carry `fundsSafu` (Depot additionally `noSupplyIncrease`). TractorFacet, which executes an arbitrary `AdvancedFarmCall[]` batch via `LibFarm._advancedFarm` (facet.delegatecall) AS THE PUBLISHER (LibTractor._user() returns blueprint.publisher inside the diamond), does NOT inherit Invariable (`contract TractorFacet` with no base) and its `tractor()` entrypoint carries only `verifyRequisition` + `runBlueprint`. It is the sole fund-executing batch entrypoint with no wrapper-level `fundsSafu`/flow guard. This is an asymmetric, incomplete guard relative to the otherwise-uniform Invariable architecture documented in Invariable.sol ('Every external writing function should use as many non-redundant invariant modifiers as possible. Excepting Diamond functions.').
impact: Defense-in-depth solvency loss on the tractor path. Each inner delegatecall into a guarded facet (deposit/withdraw/convert/claim) re-checks `fundsSafu` at its own boundary, so a single inner call cannot leave the protocol insolvent. The residual exposure is that tractor executes a publisher-authorized batch with no batch-level net check: any unguarded inner sink reachable through a blueprint (a facet selector that moves funds but lacks `fundsSafu` itself), or an interleaving that is solvent at each inner checkpoint yet net-adverse across the batch, would execute with the publisher's delegated context and no final solvency assertion. FarmFacet closes exactly this gap with a wrapper `fundsSafu`; Tractor cannot because it does not inherit Invariable.

ite.intent: Preserve the uniform Invariable solvency net across every fund-executing entrypoint, including the publisher-delegated tractor batch
ite.technique: TractorFacet is declared without `is Invariable`, so tractor() cannot and does not apply fundsSafu; the only guards are signature/nonce/time. The wrapper-level solvency assertion that FarmFacet uses is absent on the equivalent Tractor batch path.
ite.evasion: Operator submits a publisher-signed blueprint whose AdvancedFarmCall[] either reaches a fund-moving facet selector that itself lacks fundsSafu, or composes guarded calls in an order solvent at each inner checkpoint but net-adverse across the batch; no batch-level fundsSafu fires.

ice_chain.corrupted_state: Beanstalk token solvency invariant (balances[i] >= entitlements[i]) is not asserted at the tractor batch boundary
ice_chain.impact: Potential protocol-level under-collateralization executed under a publisher's delegated context without a batch-level solvency revert; concrete fund loss depends on whether a reachable inner sink lacks its own fundsSafu
ice_chain.exploit_path: tractor(blueprint) -> _setPublisher(publisher) -> for each AdvancedFarmCall: facet.delegatecall -> [no wrapper fundsSafu] -> _resetPublisher. Confirming/denying impact requires enumerating every diamond selector reachable from a blueprint and proving each fund-moving one carries its own fundsSafu; that selector-completeness proof is not closeable from source alone, so this is routed for human verification rather than cleared.
